title: arXiv Mathematics — Friday, 6 November 2026
global_caveat: arXiv publishes no official trending chart, so this is an inferred order; the papers are very new and citation evidence is limited.

sections.title: Tusnády’s problem and online two-sample thinning
sections.abstract: The author proves the sharp fixed-dimension Tusnády discrepancy order, a robust lower bound for random samples, and minimax online-thinning rates for two samples from an unknown common distribution.
sections.claimed_result: The author proves box discrepancy is Θ_d((log N)^(d−1/2)) for every fixed d≥2. For online thinning with fixed k≥1 and expected deletion budget ρn, 0<ρ<2, minimax expected prefix discrepancy is Θ_(k,ρ)((log n)^(k+1/2)); in one dimension the terminal rate is Θ_ρ((log log n)^(3/2)).
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The discrepancy order holds with dimension fixed. Thinning concerns two independent size-n samples from the same unknown Borel distribution; keep/discard choices are online and irrevocable.
sections.unique_caveat: For k≥2, the paper's terminal upper and lower bounds still differ by a factor of log n.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A dedicated Polymath Hub discussion is an independent attention signal; the result also links combinatorial discrepancy, algorithms, and probability and claims a sharp order.

sections.title: Pointless K3 surfaces over finite fields
sections.abstract: The authors prove that a K3 surface without an F_q-rational point exists if and only if q≤11, using lattice bounds, the Artin–Tate formula, and embeddings into Niemeier lattices.
sections.claimed_result: The authors’ Theorem 1 establishes existence of pointless K3 surfaces over F_q exactly for prime powers q≤11, sharpening the general Weil-bound cutoff and improving a bound used in related threefold results.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Smooth K3 surfaces over finite fields; the theorem concerns existence of at least one pointless surface for each field size.
sections.unique_caveat: The proof uses numerical linear-programming certificates and lattice computations; the authors provide code/data and describe a separate proof of the same cutoff.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The exact cutoff is independently reached in another recent arXiv paper by Brandhorst and Takada using a different approach; this convergence and number-theory/algebraic-geometry link are checkable signals.

sections.title: On do Carmo’s Question: The Properly Embedded Case
sections.abstract: The author proves that every complete, noncompact, two-sided, properly embedded constant-mean-curvature hypersurface of finite Morse index in Euclidean space is minimal, in every dimension.
sections.claimed_result: The author's main theorem says the mean curvature must vanish under the stated hypotheses. The proof uses the inscribed-ball radius to build a weight, combines a weighted-volume estimate with stability outside a compact set, and derives a contradiction if mean curvature is nonzero.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Smooth connected hypersurfaces without boundary in Euclidean space, arbitrary dimension; completeness, noncompactness, two-sidedness, proper embeddedness, and finite Morse index are required.
sections.unique_caveat: Proper embeddedness is essential to the presented argument; the broader finite-index question for general immersed hypersurfaces remains open.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A differential-geometry papers account independently highlighted it; the result is cross-listed in geometry and geometric PDE and removes curvature and volume-growth bounds in its stated setting.

sections.title: Improved Index and Intersection bounds for Min-Max Geodesics
sections.abstract: The authors improve a bound for geodesics realizing the p-widths of a closed surface, showing that the sum of their Morse indices and a count of their intersections is at most p.
sections.claimed_result: Theorem 1.2 bounds the sum of the Morse indices plus the sum, over intersection vertices, of squared vertex orders by p, for a collection of closed immersed geodesics realizing the p-width of a closed Riemannian surface.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Closed Riemannian surfaces and geodesic unions arising as p-width limits; the theorem also applies to the Allen–Cahn limit-varifold setting described by the authors.
sections.unique_caveat: The stated min-max application is for surfaces and geodesics realizing p-widths; it does not establish analogous bounds in higher ambient dimensions.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Included in a public differential-geometry papers roundup and improves the authors’ previous bound; the proof combines Jacobi-field variations with localized variations near intersection vertices.

sections.title: A stability order barrier and SSP bound for Runge–Kutta methods with non-negative coefficients: AI-assisted proofs
sections.abstract: The authors prove SSP-coefficient bounds for implicit Runge–Kutta methods with non-negative coefficients, settle a conjecture at order two, and show that third-order methods with non-negative A and b cannot be algebraically stable.
sections.claimed_result: For every s-stage implicit Runge–Kutta method of order at least two with non-negative coefficients, the SSP coefficient is at most 2s, sharply attained at order two; the paper also gives a bound for order at least three and rules out third-order algebraic stability when A and b are entrywise non-negative.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Implicit Runge–Kutta methods with non-negative coefficients; the claims have the distinct order and coefficient hypotheses stated in the paper.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors report Lean verification for elementary components and reductions, not the entire paper as a formal proof; results are restricted to the specified non-negative-coefficient classes.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A named conjecture is claimed settled; the paper documents a mathematical bridge from SSP conditions to phase-type distributions and reports partial Lean verification.

sections.title: Trending Research Themes
text: Discrepancy and online algorithms: Lei proves the fixed-dimensional sharp Tusnády order and extends it to two-sample thinning; Wengiel’s separate recent preprint also claims the sharp order. The papers use different routes.
Finite-field K3 cutoff: Auel–Engel–Kedlaya–Shaikh and Brandhorst–Takada independently give the q≤11 cutoff with differing methods; this is concentrated convergence, not evidence of a wider shift.

Separate geometric-analysis results: Niu treats finite-index CMC hypersurfaces, while Sarnataro–Stryker–Marx-Kuo improve a min-max geodesic bound on surfaces; they do not establish a shared technique.
The Runge–Kutta paper’s AI-assisted proof process and partial Lean verification are an isolated signal, not evidence of a field-wide shift.

sections.title: Open Problems and Research Directions
text: Author-stated gap: terminal online-thinning bounds for dimensions k≥2 differ by log n; seek a matching terminal algorithm or lower bound. [2611.08455]
Author-stated open case: the finite-index result for general immersed CMC hypersurfaces would follow if an appropriate positive weight could be constructed without proper embeddedness. [2611.08454]
Author-stated connection: the K3 paper leaves unexplained the relation between its Artin–Tate/lattice proof and the independent Brandhorst–Takada proof. [2611.08356, 2611.06366]
Synthesis: test whether min-max index/vertex bounds extend from surfaces to higher-dimensional minimal hypersurfaces. [2611.08450]

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.text: The clearest attention signal is the sharp discrepancy result and its online-thinning extension; the other strong entries are theorem-led, with an independent two-paper convergence on the K3 cutoff. The ordering is a qualitative inference from discussion and mathematical signals, not measured readership, and these preprints’ claims still require expert scrutiny.
